REAL DEFECT FOUND -- a reachable panic across the FFI boundary in hex_decode_32():

    if s.len() != 64 { return Err(InvalidPeerKey) }
    ... u8::from_str_radix(&s[2 * i..2 * i + 2], 16) ...

str::len() is a BYTE count, but the loop then slices that same &str by byte range. A 64-BYTE peer key containing a multi-byte UTF-8 character makes a slice endpoint land mid-character, and Rust's str range-indexing panics on a non-char-boundary index. Minimal repro: "EURO SIGN" (U+20AC, 3 bytes) followed by 61 ASCII characters is exactly 64 bytes, so it passes the length check; then &s[0..2] cuts into that 3-byte character (which occupies bytes 0..3) -> panic, "byte index 2 is not a char boundary".

Reachable from real user input, not only from a test. MainActivity.onConnectClicked() (line 217) reads peerPublicKeyInput's raw text, .trim()s it, checks only isEmpty(), and passes it straight into dialChannelDirect(), whose very first step is hex_decode_32(). A key pasted with a smart quote, an em dash or an emoji attached is enough to reach it.

The consequence is an app crash, not a handled error. native-bridge sets no panic="abort", so UniFFI's catch_unwind converts the panic into InternalException("Rust panic") (generated bindings, native_bridge.kt line 297). onConnectClicked catches only ChannelException and LinkageError, so InternalException escapes the lifecycleScope.launch coroutine uncaught and takes the app down.

This contradicts the module's own stated contract. message.rs's header states that decoding attacker-controlled or truncated bytes "must never panic across FFI"; channel.rs documents hex_decode_32 as "a real FFI input-validation boundary". The test written to guarantee exactly that -- dial_rejects_a_malformed_peer_key_without_panicking -- only passes "not-hex", 7 ASCII bytes, which the length check rejects before the slicing loop ever executes. The panic path is therefore entirely uncovered by the existing suite.

Bounded fix, contained in one function: reject non-ASCII input before slicing (or decode from s.as_bytes() chunks instead of str byte ranges), plus a regression test using a 64-byte non-ASCII key.

Minor, same function, reported for completeness: u8::from_str_radix accepts a leading '+', so the pair "+f" parses as 0x0f -- input that is not strictly hexadecimal is accepted. No security impact today, because dial_channel_direct re-encodes the decoded bytes canonically before they ever reach sender_pubkey.

      messagesText.text = if (messagesText.text.isEmpty()) line else "${messagesText.text}\n$line"
   That reads the whole accumulated transcript back out of the TextView and re-concatenates it for EVERY message, so rendering N messages costs O(N^2) time and O(N^2) allocation -- and each step additionally triggers a full setText() -> re-measure/re-layout of the entire text block. loadPersistedHistory() then drives exactly that in `history.forEach { renderMessage(...) }`, which runs on the main dispatcher (only the loadAll() call itself is inside withContext(Dispatchers.IO)).
